title: ATS Resume Test: Check Your CV for Nigerian Job Applications
excerpt: Learn how to test your resume for ATS compatibility and improve your chances with Nigerian employers using automated screening systems.
author: ElevateResume

body.text: In Nigeria's competitive job market, over 75% of large companies like Dangote Group, MTN Nigeria, and Access Bank use Applicant Tracking Systems (ATS) to screen resumes before human recruiters ever see them. If your CV isn't ATS-optimized, it might never reach hiring managers, regardless of your qualifications.

An ATS resume test helps you identify and fix issues that could prevent your application from passing automated screening. This comprehensive guide will show you exactly how to test your resume for ATS compatibility and optimize it for Nigerian job applications.
What is an ATS Resume Test?

An ATS resume test is a process that evaluates how well your CV performs when scanned by applicant tracking systems. These tests simulate the automated screening process used by Nigerian companies to filter job applications.

items: Keyword optimization and relevance
Formatting compatibility
Section organization and headers
Contact information accessibility
File format appropriateness
Overall readability score

body.text: Companies like Nigerian Breweries, Lafarge Africa, and Unilever Nigeria rely heavily on ATS to manage thousands of applications. A poorly optimized resume might score below 60%, automatically eliminating you from consideration.
Why ATS Testing Matters for Nigerian Job Seekers
Nigerian employers receive an average of 200-500 applications per job posting, especially for popular positions in Lagos, Abuja, and Port Harcourt. ATS helps them manage this volume efficiently by:

items: Automatically ranking candidates based on keyword matches
Filtering out improperly formatted resumes
Identifying relevant experience and skills
Shortlisting top candidates for human review

body.text: Without proper ATS optimization, qualified candidates often miss opportunities at top Nigerian companies including:

items: Banking sector: GTBank, First Bank, UBA
Telecommunications: Airtel, 9mobile, Glo
Oil & Gas: Shell Nigeria, Total, Chevron
Manufacturing: Nestle Nigeria, PZ Cussons, Cadbury

body.text: Common ATS Resume Problems in Nigeria
Many Nigerian job seekers use overly complex CV templates that confuse ATS systems:

items: **Tables and columns**: ATS often reads these incorrectly
**Graphics and images**: Cannot be processed by most systems
**Unusual fonts**: May not render properly in ATS
**Text boxes**: Content might be skipped entirely
**Generic language**: Using vague terms instead of industry-specific keywords
**Missing variations**: Not including different forms of the same skill
**Location gaps**: Failing to mention Nigerian cities where you're willing to work
**Currency confusion**: Using foreign currency symbols instead of Naira

body.text: When applying for positions in Nigerian banks, include keywords like "Core Banking," "Treasury Management," "Risk Assessment," and "CBN regulations" to improve your ATS score.
Optimizing Your Resume for ATS Success
Structure your resume with clear, standard headings that ATS can easily identify:

items: **Contact Information**
**Professional Summary** or **Career Objective**
**Work Experience** or **Professional Experience**
**Education** or **Academic Qualifications**
**Skills** or **Core Competencies**
**Certifications** (especially important in Nigeria)
**Professional Memberships** (ICAN, NBA, NSE, etc.)
Clearly state your NYSC status and year of service
Mention state of service if relevant to the job location
Use full university names ("University of Lagos" not "UNILAG")
Include both local and international degree equivalents
Specify willingness to relocate within Nigeria
Mention familiarity with different Nigerian business environments
Highlight relevant professional certifications (CIPM, ICAN, CISA)
Include ongoing certification progress
**PDF**: Best for maintaining formatting integrity
**Word (.docx)**: Preferred by some older ATS systems
**Avoid**: .pages, .txt, or image formats

Testing Against Specific Nigerian Job Descriptions
When applying for banking positions in Nigeria, test your resume against keywords commonly found in job postings:

items: Technical skills: Core banking systems, SWIFT, anti-money laundering
Soft skills: Customer relationship management, risk assessment
Regulatory knowledge: CBN guidelines, Basel III compliance
Experience: Branch operations, credit analysis, treasury management

body.text: For tech positions with companies like Interswitch, Flutterwave, or SystemSpecs:

items: Programming languages: Java, Python, JavaScript, C#
Frameworks: React, Angular, Laravel, Django
Methodologies: Agile, Scrum, DevOps
Tools: Git, Docker, Kubernetes, AWS
**80-100%**: Excellent ATS compatibility
**60-79%**: Good with minor improvements needed
**40-59%**: Moderate issues requiring attention
**Below 40%**: Significant optimization required

body.text: 1. **Keyword Match Rate**: Percentage of job posting keywords found in your resume
2. **Readability Score**: How easily ATS can parse your content
4. **Section Recognition**: Whether ATS identifies all resume sections

items: Using creative templates with complex layouts
Including headers and footers with important information
Employing non-standard section names
Adding watermarks or background images
Stuffing keywords unnaturally into text
Using abbreviations without spelling out full terms
Failing to quantify achievements with specific metrics
Omitting relevant Nigerian business context

body.text: Nigerian employers particularly value quantified achievements. Instead of "improved sales," write "increased sales by 25% within 6 months, contributing ₦2.5 million to quarterly revenue."

items: **Oil & Gas**: Emphasize safety certifications and international standards

**Telecommunications**: Focus on technical certifications and project management
